subject: chemistry
title: The process of electrolysis
key_idea: An electrolyte is an ionic compound that is molten or dissolved in water, so its ions are free to move. In electrolysis, a direct current makes positive ions move to the negative electrode and negative ions move to the positive electrode, where they are discharged as elements.

blocks.text: This section covers which substances can be electrolysed and why.

items.meaning: An ionic compound, molten or dissolved in water, that conducts electricity because its ions can move.
Using electrical energy from a direct current supply to break down an electrolyte.
A rod that carries the current into or out of the electrolyte.

columns: Are the ions free to move?
rows: No. The ions are in fixed positions in the lattice.
No. It does not dissolve, so the ions stay fixed.

items: **Ions**, not electrons, carry the charge through an electrolyte.
A covalent compound such as glucose has no ions, so its solution does not conduct. A lamp in the circuit stays unlit.
To test a solution, put two electrodes in it and connect them to a supply. A lamp that lights, or an ammeter reading, shows that it conducts.
An electrolyte is an ionic compound that is molten or dissolved in water.
A solid ionic compound does not conduct because its ions cannot move.

blocks.text: This section covers how ions move and what happens to them at the electrodes.

items: A **direct current** is passed through the electrolyte.
Positive ions (cations) move to the negative electrode, the cathode.
Negative ions (anions) move to the positive electrode, the anode.
Opposite charges attract, so each ion moves towards the electrode with the opposite charge.
At the electrode the ions are **discharged**. They gain or lose electrons and form elements.

blocks.text: In a coloured solution you can see this. A coloured ion moves towards the electrode with the opposite charge, and the colour appears there.
Which ion is discharged at each electrode is covered in the notes on molten compounds and aqueous solutions. Half equations are in the Higher tier note.

checks.q: Explain why solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity but molten sodium chloride does.
checks.a: In the solid the ions are in fixed positions and cannot move. When molten, the ions are free to move and carry the charge.

checks.q: Which electrode do positive ions move to, and why?
checks.a: The negative electrode (cathode), because opposite charges attract.

checks.q: State what is meant by electrolysis.
checks.a: Electrical energy (from a direct current supply) breaks down (decomposes) an electrolyte, which is an ionic compound.

exam_phrases: (so are) attracted to the negative electrode
chromate ions moved to the positive electrode
(negative ions) are attracted to the positive electrode

mistakes.wrong: The solution turned yellow because the ions moved.
mistakes.right: Two separate marks are given. Name the ion and its direction: yellow chromate ions moved to the positive electrode. Then give the reason: opposite charges attract.

mistakes.wrong: Sodium chloride also conducts electricity when it is dissolved.
mistakes.right: References to aqueous solutions and to dissolving are ignored when the solution is already given. The other state is liquid or molten.

worked_example.question: Explain why copper ions (Cu²⁺) move to the negative electrode.
answer_points: So they are attracted to the negative electrode.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the charge on the ion and one for the attraction. 'Opposite charges attract' is also accepted.

exam_phrases: electrical energy / electricity decomposes / breaks down electrolytes / (ionic) compounds
it contains ions that can move
in solution ions can move / in solid ions cannot move
(calcium carbonate is) insoluble so ions are not free to move

mistakes.wrong: Electrolysis is the decomposition of elements by electricity.
mistakes.right: Decomposing elements is rejected. Electrolysis decomposes electrolytes, which are ionic compounds.

mistakes.wrong: Solid copper chloride does not conduct because its electrons cannot move.
mistakes.right: Electrons, atoms and molecules are rejected. Say the ions cannot move because they are held in a lattice, so no current flows. 'Nothing happens' is not accepted.

mistakes.wrong: Calcium carbonate mixed with water is not an electrolyte because it has no ions.
mistakes.right: It does contain ions. It is insoluble, so the ions are not free to move. Calcium nitrate dissolves, so its ions can move.

worked_example.question:
A student investigated whether electricity can pass through solid ammonium chloride and through ammonium chloride solution. If an electrical current flows in the circuit, the lamp will light up.

Results:
solid ammonium chloride: the lamp did not light up
ammonium chloride solution: the lamp lit up brightly

Explain the results of the investigation.
answer_points: Ammonium chloride solution conducts electricity and solid ammonium chloride does not.
In solution the ions can move. In the solid the ions cannot move.
worked_example.tip: Refer to both the solid and the solution to score full marks.

exam_phrases: ions are free to move in aqueous solution
ionic (type of compound in an electrolyte)

mistakes.wrong: Sodium chloride conducts when dissolved because its electrons can move.
mistakes.right: Electrons moving is not allowed. In solution the ions are free to move, and the ions carry the charge.

mistakes.wrong: Sodium chloride solution contains only Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
mistakes.right: Water also supplies H⁺ and OH⁻. The positive ions (cations) are Na⁺ and H⁺. The negative ions (anions) are Cl⁻ and OH⁻.

worked_example.question:
Javier is electrolysing a solution of sodium chloride, NaCl, in water, H₂O.

Complete the list of ions present in sodium chloride solution.

Positive ions (cations): Na⁺ and ______
Negative ions (anions): ______ and OH⁻
worked_example.tip: The H⁺ and OH⁻ ions come from the water.
